confirmedFindings.quote: the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau's Number 1 Blue Label is the top grade
confirmedFindings.issue: "Number 1 Blue Label" is pinned to the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau as a specific named grade/mark in 4+ places (introParagraphs[1], detailedAnalysis[0].content[1], faqs[1].answer). The string "Number 1 Blue Label" appears in NO fact pack — only in the draft's own GAPS doc. The historic-restoration pack explicitly bans this: line 248-249 lists "naming a specific CSSB certification mark ... not verified to the Bureau" as Banned and directs stating it qualitatively as "grades and installation standards published by the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau," and GAP #7 (lines 418-423) repeats that the exact mark names "were not verified to a primary Bureau source ... do not name a specific mark unless verified." Line 244 confirms the Bureau only as the named grading/installation authority. The draft GAPS #7 defends keeping it as a "denotative formal grade name," but that is overridden by the pack's explicit named caution. This is over-attribution of an unverified mark to a named source.
confirmedFindings.fix: Drop the unverified mark name and state grade authority qualitatively. introParagraphs[1]: "the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau's Number 1 Blue Label is the top grade" → "the top grades use all-heartwood, edge-grain stock, graded against the standards the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau publishes." faqs[1].answer: "The Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau's Number 1 Blue Label is the top cedar grade, using all-heartwood, edge-grain stock for the longest service life." → "The top cedar grades use all-heartwood, edge-grain stock for the longest service life, graded against the standards the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau publishes." Apply the same de-marking to detailedAnalysis[0].content[1] (see F4).
confirmedFindings.refuteReason: Survives: facts-historic-restoration.md lines 248-249 and 418-423 explicitly BAN naming a specific unverified CSSB mark and mandate qualitative phrasing; line 244 attributes to the Bureau only the grading/installation authority. A full grep of facts-historic-restoration.md and facts-materials-economics.md returns "Number 1 Blue Label" in ZERO pack lines (only in the draft's own GAPS doc). The mark is unsourced and explicitly named-cautioned, so the GAPS 'denotative grade name' defense does not hold.

confirmedFindings.quote: shakes run 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick against shingles' thinner sawn profile and last 20–40 years
confirmedFindings.issue: The shake-thickness figure "1/2 to 3/4 inch thick" is an unsourced hard dimensional number. facts-materials-economics.md §5 (lines 209-235) carries the cedar lifespans (shake 20-40, shingle 30-50, CSSB), failure modes, the ≥1.5 in. air-space figure, the flex test, and repair/maintenance costs — but NO unit thickness. facts-historic-restoration.md §5 carries no shake-thickness dimension either. Hard numeric claims must trace to a pack or be stated qualitatively; this one does not. The thicker-vs-thinner contrast itself IS supported by §5 / directAnswer; only the 1/2-3/4 in. number is invented.
confirmedFindings.fix: Drop the unsourced dimension, keep the sourced thicker-vs-thinner contrast qualitatively. Before: "shakes run 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick against shingles' thinner sawn profile and last 20–40 years, per the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau." → After: "shakes are the thicker, hand-split or taper-sawn unit against shingles' thinner sawn profile and last 20–40 years, per the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau."
confirmedFindings.refuteReason: Survives: a grep of facts-materials-economics.md §5 (lines 209-235) and facts-historic-restoration.md returns no "1/2", "3/4", or any cedar unit-thickness dimension; the packs carry only lifespans, failure modes, ≥1.5 in. air space, and costs. The numeric thickness is unsourced; the qualitative thicker/thinner contrast is independently supported and is retained.

confirmedFindings.quote: Untreated western red cedar silvers within months of NJ exposure as UV weathers the surface, per the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau
confirmedFindings.issue: The silvering/graying claim is pinned to the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau, but NO pack carries any silvering or graying statement (CSSB or otherwise). facts-materials-economics.md §5 line 219 attributes to CSSB/NRCA only cupping/warping, edge splitting, rot, and moss/algae — not graying. The draft GAPS #6 already flagged the original "6–12 months" window as unsourced and softened the timing, but the fix retained the unsupported "per the CSSB" attribution for a graying claim the pack never makes. This is over-attribution. The HomeGuide maintenance attribution in the second sentence IS valid (§5 line 235: fungicide/algaecide $0.15–$0.60/sq ft, HomeGuide).
confirmedFindings.fix: State the UV-weathering mechanism qualitatively and drop the unsupported CSSB attribution for the graying. Before: "Untreated western red cedar silvers within months of NJ exposure as UV weathers the surface, per the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau. A UV-inhibiting preservative reapplied with the fungicide-algaecide cycle slows the graying, per HomeGuide." → After: "Untreated western red cedar weathers to a silver-gray as UV degrades the surface. A UV-inhibiting preservative reapplied with the fungicide-algaecide cycle slows the graying, per HomeGuide." (Keep the HomeGuide attribution; remove the unsupported CSSB tag from the graying claim.)
confirmedFindings.refuteReason: Survives: a grep of all research packs returns no silvering/graying claim attributed to the CSSB (or any source); facts-materials-economics.md §5 line 219 lists the CSSB/NRCA failure modes as cupping/splitting/rot/moss-algae only. The "per the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau" tag on the graying claim is unsupported. The HomeGuide maintenance attribution retained in the fix is confirmed at §5 line 235.

confirmedFindings.quote: sold in hand-split-and-resawn and taper-sawn grades graded to the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau's Number 1 Blue Label, hand-split, and taper-sawn standards
confirmedFindings.issue: Garbled, redundant phrasing: the clause lists "hand-split-and-resawn and taper-sawn grades," then re-lists "hand-split, and taper-sawn standards" in the same sentence — a double-naming that reads as an assembly artifact — and conflates a grade name (Number 1 Blue Label) with cut types (hand-split, taper-sawn) as if all three were grading "standards." Compounds F1, which removes the unverified mark name.
confirmedFindings.fix: Rewrite cleanly without the duplication and without the unverified mark. Before: "sold in hand-split-and-resawn and taper-sawn grades graded to the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau's Number 1 Blue Label, hand-split, and taper-sawn standards." → After: "sold as hand-split-and-resawn or taper-sawn product, graded against the standards the Cedar Shake & Shingle Bureau publishes."
confirmedFindings.refuteReason: Survives: the sentence demonstrably double-lists "hand-split ... and taper-sawn" (once as grades, once as standards) and mislabels the cut types and the mark name jointly as Bureau "standards" — a genuine assembly-artifact garble independent of sourcing, and it carries the same unverified "Number 1 Blue Label" mark the pack bans (facts-historic-restoration.md lines 248-249 / 418-423).
